rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement “no deity but He” negates every supposed god; its omitted predicate can be “exists” or “is,” with “deity” meaning a real deity.
rows.anchor: المراد بالإله ما يصدق عليه الإله حقيقة وواقعا، وحينئذ فيصح أن يكون الخبر المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because “Allah” is nominative, illa is descriptive (meaning “other than”), not an exception: no deity other than Allah exists.
rows.anchor: فلفظ إلا ليس للاستثناء، بل وصف بمعنى غير، والمعنى لا إله، غير الله بموجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause excludes imagined rivals rather than proving God exists; the context needs only denial of other deities, since the Qur’an treats God's existence as self-evident and argues for His attributes.
rows.anchor: مسوقة لنفي غير الله من الآلهة الموهومة المتخيلة لا لنفي غير الله وإثبات وجود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says this parsing denies an actual rival’s existence but not its possibility; one reply is that no merely possible being could ground all actual existence and its properties.
rows.anchor: لا معنى لفرض موجود ممكن مساوي الوجود والعدم ينتهي إليه وجود جميع الموجودات بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed parsing supplies “true”: there is no true object of worship except God.
rows.anchor: وربما يجاب عنه بتقدير حق، والمعنى لا معبود حق إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm complete lordship: God gives universal gifts through the first and gifts guiding creatures to final, afterlife happiness through the second.
rows.anchor: بذكر الاسمين يتم معنى الربوبية، فإليه تعالى ينتهي كل عطية عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in this verse demonstrate the preceding claims that the human community has one God, who is universally merciful and guides toward ultimate happiness.
rows.anchor: الآية مسوقة للدلالة والبرهنة على ما تضمنته الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing cosmos maintains one connected, ordered system: both its assembled whole and its smallest parts display continuous governance, though each entity differs in nature and properties; this points to one creator and governor (his second proof).
rows.anchor: فالعالم شيء واحد والتدبير متصل، وجميع الأجزاء مسخرة تحت نظام واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth-dwelling humans depend for material life on the connected cosmic order, including celestial light and heat, day and night, wind, clouds, and rain; their creator and governor is therefore the same God (his third proof).
rows.anchor: فهذه الأجرام العلوية في إنارتها وتسخينها، وهذه الأرض في اختلاف ليلها ونهارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same God grants what creatures need for present and final happiness: the afterlife follows this world, so its governor must be the governor of this life; this establishes the names al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm.
rows.anchor: فإن الآخرة عقبى هذا الدار، وكيف يمكن أن يدبر عاقبة الأمر غير الذي يدبر نفس الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening inna signals that verse 164 explains and establishes the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وفي تصدير الآية بلفظة، إن الدالة على التعليل إشارة إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Creating the heavens and earth” includes their diverse structures, forms, materials, transformations, growth and decline; he links these processes to two other Qur’anic passages.
rows.anchor: أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night–day variation arises from Earth’s daily rotation and the inclination of its equatorial plane relative to its orbital plane, which shifts the Sun north and south and produces seasons.
rows.anchor: وهي الحركة اليومية التي للأرض على مركزها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the poles each solar year has one day and one night, each about half a year; at the equator day and night are roughly equal, while other regions vary with latitude.
rows.anchor: أما القطبان فلهما في كل سنة شمسية تامة يوم وليلة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing day length alters light and heat and thus the conditions that produce varied terrestrial forms and transformations useful to humans.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاختلاف هو الموجب لاختلاف ورود الضوء والحرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falak means a ship and can denote one or several; its benefit is carrying goods and provisions between shores and regions.
rows.anchor: والفلك هو السفينة يطلق على الواحد والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships, like other natural entities, depend on God for existence and governance; the Qur’an calls ships His property and says He subjects them to sail by His command.
rows.anchor: فالفلك أيضا مثل سائر الموجودات الطبيعية تفتقر إلى الإله في وجودها

rows.speaker: الماديون
rows.claim: Materialists argue that belief in a creator arose because early people could not identify material causes; as science explains those events, they expect it eventually to explain spiritual life too and remove the need for a creator.
rows.anchor: وهم أصحاب المادة من المنكرين لوجود الصانع - زعموا أن حجة المليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects treating human-made things as detached from God merely because human choice produces them; human agency remains dependent on God like natural causes.
rows.anchor: فما أغفل هؤلاء الذين يعدون الصناعيات من الأشياء التي يعملها الإنسان

rows.speaker: المثبتون
rows.claim: Believers in a creator have long affirmed one or many makers of the whole world; the Qur’an presents monotheism as earlier than idolatry, and Max Müller is cited on the antiquity of belief in a creator.
rows.anchor: فالمثبتون - ولم يقدر البحث والتاريخ على تعيين مبدأ لظهورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theists do not posit God only to fill gaps in knowledge: they hold that the entire connected world, including known natural causal chains, depends on a cause beyond that chain.
rows.anchor: لإذعانهم بأن هذا العالم المؤلف من سلسلة علل ومعلولات طبيعية بمجموعها ووحدانيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He points out the materialists’ inconsistency: they accept determinism for all events, including human actions, yet suppose that human creation could escape dependence on the world's first cause.
rows.anchor: ومن عجيب المناقضة في كلام هؤلاء أنهم قائلون في الحوادث

rows.speaker: الحكماء الباحثين
rows.claim: Philosophical proofs begin from universal causality and argue that possible causes must ultimately depend on a Necessary Existent; they apply this even where a natural cause is known.
rows.anchor: البراهين العقلية التي أقامتها الالهيون من الحكماء الباحثين أقاموها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an affirms universal causation: it attributes natural events and human choices to their proximate agents, while also attributing every thing to God.
rows.anchor: فكل ما صدق عليه اسم شيء فهو مخلوق لله منسوب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some verses attribute an act both to its human agent and to God, as with human work and the Prophet’s throwing; this preserves both levels of attribution.
rows.anchor: فنسب أعمال الناس إليهم ونسب خلق أنفسهم وأعمالهم إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creation of each thing includes delimiting it by material causes and temporal and spatial conditions; the Qur’an repeatedly describes creation as measured.
rows.anchor: فإن تقدير كل شيء هو جعله محدودا بحدود العلل المادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an does not assign only unexplained events to God while leaving explained events solely to material causes; all causation ultimately depends on God.
rows.anchor: لا كما يزعمه هؤلاء من إسناد البعض إلى الله وإسناد الآخر إلى علله المادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He traces these mistaken arguments to a distorted, weak popular theology inherited from medieval church philosophy and other theologians, which denied divine dependence for known causes and human choices.
rows.anchor: فلسفة عامية كانت تنشرها الكنيسة في القرون الوسطى

rows.speaker: بعض المحدثين والمتكلمين
rows.claim: Some hadith scholars, literalist theologians, and others deny that human-made products, especially objects made for sinful uses such as wine and gambling tools, are attributable to God because the Qur’an calls them Satan’s work.
rows.anchor: بعض المحدثين والمتكلمين من ظاهريي المسلمين وجمع من غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human crafts depend on God as do natural things. An idol’s material existence is God-created, while its status as an object worshipped besides God belongs to human or satanic action.
rows.anchor: فإن الصنم ليس بحسب الحقيقة إلا حجرا أو فلزا عليه شكل خاص وليس فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manufactured things are attributable to creation just like natural things, in proportion to their existence.
rows.anchor: الأمور الصناعية منتسبة إلى الخلقة كاستناد الأمور الطبيعية من غير فرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain develops through evaporation, condensation and precipitation as rain, snow, or hail; it nourishes Earth and sustains plants and animals, and, as part of the connected world, points to one creator who is also humanity’s God.
rows.anchor: ماء البحار وغيره ثم يتكاثف بخارا متصاعدا حاملا للحرارة حتى ينتهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind is air displaced by unequal solar heating: warmed, lighter air rises as cooler, heavier air moves in and pushes it along; wind pollinates plants, disperses vapor and decay, and carries rain clouds.
rows.anchor: ومن منافعه تلقيح النبات ودفع الكثافات البخارية، والعفونات المتصاعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cloud is condensed vapor that yields rain; vapor near the ground is called fog, and higher vapor is cloud or related terms. Its movement and rainfall are subdued by wind, cold, and other forces by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: والسحاب مسخر مقهور في سيره وإمطاره بالريح والبرودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night–day cycle, rain, wind, and clouds are the general processes composing the terrestrial order; this verse details in one respect the provision described in another verse.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية كالتفصيل بوجه لإجمال قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aql means complete understanding; as a faculty of discernment it is the perceiving human self, not a subsidiary power like sight or memory.
rows.anchor: وهو نفس الإنسان المدرك وليس بقوة من قواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind’s existence points to God; its integration with other things points to one God for the world, and its role in human life points to the same God for humans and the rest of creation.
rows.anchor: وهو في وجوده يدل على الإله وفي التئامه مع سائر الموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “beside God” recalls the preceding declaration that God alone is deity: those who take rivals knowingly violate that claim and follow desire, so the text belittles them.
rows.anchor: لأن المقام مسبوق بالحصر في قوله { وإلهكم إله واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They love them” shows that rivals include not only idols but angels, humans treated as lords, and any being obeyed without God’s authorization.
rows.anchor: بل يشمل الملائكه، وأفرادا من الإنسان الذين اتخذوهم أربابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love is a conscious, special attraction between a person and a perfection; experience indicates that animals also love, and non-animals can do so where they receive or impart a perfection with awareness.
rows.anchor: إن الحب تعلق خاص وانجذاب مخصوص شعوري بين الإنسان وبين كماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love connects lover and beloved in existence; a conscious effect would itself love its cause if it had a soul and independent being.
rows.anchor: لما كان الحب تعلقا وجوديا بين المحب والمحبوب كانت رابطة قائمة بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People love their own acts and what those acts involve: food, spouses, possessions, status, benefactors, teachers, guides, helpers, students, servants, and others who obey them; these loves may be natural, imaginative, or intellectual.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا كنا نحب أفعالنا لاستكمالنا بها ونحب ما يتعلق به أفعالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love has degrees of strength because it is an existential relation, and the perfection involved can be necessary or optional, material or immaterial.
rows.anchor: أن الحب ذو مراتب مختلفة من الشدة والضعف فأنه رابطة وجودية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported theory reduces love ultimately to desire for food; another reduces it to sexual desire. The author’s account of multiple kinds and degrees rejects both reductions.
rows.anchor: حتى ذكر بعضهم أن أصله حب الغذاء، وغيره ينحل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is worthy of love because God has infinite perfection while every other perfection is finite and existentially dependent on Him.
rows.anchor: فإنه تعالى في نفسه موجود ذو كمال غير متناه وأي كمال فرض غيره فهو متناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is also loved as the giver of blessings without limit in number or duration.
rows.anchor: وهو تعالى خالق لنا منعم علينا بنعم غير متناهية العدة والمدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because love is an existential relation within the lover’s being, everything loves itself and what follows from what it loves; God loves creation for His own sake and because creatures receive His gifts and guidance.
rows.anchor: يحب خلقه لحب ذاته، ويحب خلقه لقبولهم إنعامه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love does not intrinsically require awareness: that requirement concerns ordinary instances, whereas the existential relation itself also makes unconscious natural powers tend toward their effects.
rows.anchor: وخامسا أن لزوم الشعور والعلم في مورد الحب إنما هو بحسب المصداق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Objections to endless punishment appeal to infinite mercy, the impossibility of perpetual coercion, finite sins, the damned’s contribution to the world’s order, and the idea that punishment would be revenge despite God’s self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: فهذه وأمثالها وجوه من الإشكال أوردوها على خلود العذاب وعدم انقطاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers generally that lasting punishment is the effect of a person’s settled wretched character, acquired through choices and prior conditions; once that form is complete, its fitting effects follow necessarily.
rows.anchor: فإن العذاب الخالد أثر وخاصة لصورة الشقاء الذي لزمت الإنسان الشقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine mercy is not emotional pity but giving what a recipient’s fully formed readiness calls for; general mercy grants existence and fitting results, while special mercy guides toward unity and nearness.
rows.anchor: بل معناها العطية والإفاضة لما يناسب الاستعداد التام الحاصل في القابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eternal punishment does not contradict mercy: it belongs to general mercy, while the wretched are outside the path of special mercy; otherwise the objection would also apply to temporary worldly punishment.
rows.anchor: وأما الرحمة الخاصة فلا معنى لشمولها لمن هو خارج عن صراطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes alien coercion from effects caused by a disposition that became intrinsic through repeated states; the resulting suffering fits the acquired character even while remaining unwelcome to experience.
rows.anchor: والجواب عن الثاني أنه ينبغي أن يحرر معنى عدم ملاءمة الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finite sins are preparatory causes of the settled form of wretchedness, not the direct cause of endless torment; limited causes can establish a form whose effects endure, as human form continues to produce effects after its formation.
rows.anchor: والجواب عن الثالث أن العذاب في الحقيقة ترتب أثر غير مرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Service has a general existential kind, whose recompense is general mercy (including lasting bliss or punishment), and a specific obedience on the path of unity, whose recompense is special mercy and paradise.
rows.anchor: والجواب عن الرابع أن الخدمة والعبودية أيضا مثل الرحمة على قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s relation to punishment is the same dependence on Him that applies to every existent, not a need for revenge or emotional satisfaction; punishment may still be called requital for rebellion.
rows.anchor: والجواب عن الخامس أن العذاب الدائم مستند إلى صورة الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an also presents punishment and gratitude as gifts tied to human intent and effort, supporting the account of punishment as a fitting consequence; further verses will be discussed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: فالآية كما ترى يجعل العذاب والشكر كليهما من العطية والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥlāl means making permissible. Rifth is explicit sexual speech, used here euphemistically for intercourse; the Qur’an and ordinary Arabic use other intercourse terms euphemistically too. The preposition ilā reportedly conveys approaching or giving oneself over.
rows.anchor: والرفث هو التصريح بما يكنى عنه مما يستقبح ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They are clothing for you” is a metaphor: spouses cover one another’s vulnerability and keep one another from public sexual wrongdoing. A spouse’s clothing cannot conceal that spouse from the other, fitting the permission for marital intimacy.
rows.anchor: فإن كلا من الزوجين يمنع صاحبه عن اتباع الفجور وإشاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated form of “you were betraying yourselves” suggests an ongoing practice; together, “repented” and “forgave” strongly imply that night intercourse had previously been forbidden, which this verse abrogated.
rows.anchor: فتدل الآية على أن هذه الخيانة كانت دائرة مستمرة بين المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of commentators holds that the verse abrogated the former prohibition of intercourse during Ramadan nights.
rows.anchor: كما ذكره جمع من المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative view, supported by some Sunni reports, says Muslims inferred from the comparison with earlier communities that Ramadan fasting rules matched theirs: they could eat and have sex early at night but stopped after sleeping, a burden that led to secret violations and this concession.
rows.anchor: فهموا منه التساوي في الأحكام من جميع الجهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that alternative, the comparison with earlier communities concerns the basic obligation to fast, not every detail of fasting law.
rows.anchor: التشبيه في أصل فرض الصوم لا في خصوصياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative view says “made lawful” need not imply a prior ban, since sea game was not forbidden to those in consecration; it also interprets “betraying yourselves” as supposed sin or deprivation, with repentance and pardon not explicit proof of a prohibition.
rows.anchor: أن صيد البحر لم يكن محرما على المحرمين قبل نزول الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the alternative because the wording strongly indicates a previous ban; “now approach them” follows a prohibition, and the Prophet could have conveyed fasting restrictions before this verse, allowing it to abrogate his ruling.
rows.anchor: إذ لو لم يكن هناك إلا جواز مستمر قبل نزول الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that if spouses being clothing for each other explains permission for intercourse, it cannot explain an abrogation, since it applies both before and after the verse.
rows.anchor: يدل على سبب تشريع جواز الرفث، فلا بد أن لا يعم الناسخ والمنسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers that the clothing metaphor also applies during the day, when fasting prohibits intercourse; it therefore does not alone explain the rule’s limits.
rows.anchor: مع أن حكم اللباس جار في النهار كالليل وهو محرم في النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads three conditions as nested rationales: marriage permits intimacy generally; fasting restricts it during the day; hardship and repeated violations justify restoring permission at night. Thus the rationale concerns only the new night-time concession.
rows.anchor: كون أحد الزوجين لباسا للآخر يوجب أن يجوز الرفث بينهما مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clothing relationship gives general permission for marital intimacy, fasting restricts that permission during the day, and the burden and recurring breaches justify a night concession; the verse restores only part of the general permission.
rows.anchor: وأردنا التخفيف عنكم رأفة ورحمة، وأعدنا إطلاق ذلك الحكم عليه في ليلة الصيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Now approach them” follows a prohibition and therefore commands permission; “seek what God prescribed for you” means seeking offspring, which God wrote into human nature through sexual desire, as eating naturally serves life even when people seek pleasure.
rows.anchor: والمراد بابتغاء ما كتب الله هو طلب الولد الذي كتب الله سبحانه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He finds the proposal that “what God prescribed” means a legal license unlikely, because the Qur’an does not use “writing” to mean permissibility or dispensation.
rows.anchor: فيبعده ان الكتابة في كلامه غير معهودة في مورد الحلية والرخصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are two dawns: the false dawn is a temporary vertical beam; the true dawn appears when the Sun is 18 degrees below the eastern horizon and spreads horizontally, announcing daylight.
rows.anchor: وهو الفجر الثاني ويسمى الفجر الصادق لصدقه فيما يحكيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white thread is true dawn, “from” is explanatory, and the black thread is a metaphor for the adjoining darkness; the deadline is the first appearance of true dawn, before daylight erases both threads.
rows.anchor: ان المراد بالخيط الأبيض هو الفجر الصادق، وان كلمة من، بيانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the dawn boundary is explicit, the verse concisely says to complete the fast until night; its use of “complete” treats fasting as one simple act, unlike “perfect,” which describes a composite whose parts each have an effect.
rows.anchor: أن الأول انتهاء وجود ما لا يتألف من أجزاء ذوات آثار والثاني انتهاء وجود ما لكل من أجزائه أثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtikāf means remaining in a place; as a worship, it requires staying in a mosque, leaving only for need, and fasting, so the verse bars intercourse during it despite the general night permission.
rows.anchor: والاعتكاف عبادة خاصة من أحكامها لزوم المسجد وعدم الخروج منه إلا لعذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “boundary” fundamentally prevents passage; “do not approach them” figuratively forbids either committing the listed acts or violating the fasting rules and sacred limits.
rows.anchor: والنهي عن القرب من الحدود كناية عن عدم اقترافها والتعدي إليها

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report attributed to al-Ṣādiq says intercourse was prohibited throughout Ramadan, while food was forbidden after sleeping; Khawwat b. Jubayr fell asleep before iftar, fainted while digging the trench next day, and the verse permitted night intercourse and food until dawn.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي عن الصادق عليه السلام قال كان الأكل والنكاح محرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase explaining the account beginning “and there was a man” is the narrator’s gloss; other reports in al-Kulayni and al-ʿAyyāshī likewise link the food rule to Khawwat and the sex concession to young men’s secret conduct.
rows.anchor: من كلام الراوي، وهذا المعنى مروي بروايات أخرى، رواها الكليني والعياشي

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: A report says sleepers who missed iftar could not eat that night or the following day; Qays b. Ṣirma worked while fasting, slept before eating, then fainted, and the verse brought relief.
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب قال كان أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذا كان الرجل صائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Versions vary on the name in Qays’s story, giving Abu Qubays b. Ṣirma or Ṣirma b. Mālik; the report is transmitted in multiple routes.
rows.anchor: وفي بعضها أبو قبيس بن صرمة وفي بعضها صرمه بن مالك الأنصاري

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Muslims who had prayed ʿishāʾ were forbidden food and sex until the next evening; some, including ʿUmar, transgressed and complained, so “now approach them” meant have intercourse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ان المسلمين كانوا في شهر رمضان إذا صلوا العشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most reports through Sunni transmitters say intercourse followed the same rule as food and drink: all were allowed early in the night but forbidden after sleep.
rows.anchor: وفي أكثرها اسم من عمر، وهي متحدة في أن حكم النكاح بالليل كحكم الأكل والشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first report says sex was forbidden throughout Ramadan, unlike food and drink, which were permitted before sleep; the verse’s syntax supports it because food has an explicit dawn limit while sex has none.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما اشتمل عليه بعض الروايات أن الخيانة ما كانت تختص بالنكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that violations involved food and drink as well as intercourse conflicts with the verse’s order, which places “you were betraying yourselves” before the food permission.
rows.anchor: بعض الروايات أن الخيانة ما كانت تختص بالنكاح بل كانوا يختانون

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report distinguishes a wolf-tail-like false dawn, which changes no rule, from the horizontal dawn, which permits prayer and prohibits food.
rows.anchor: الفجر فجران فأما الذي كأنه ذنب السرحان فإنه لا يحل شيئا ولا يحرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from both Sunni and Shia routes are abundant on the two dawns and on the prohibition of intercourse during iʿtikāf.
rows.anchor: والروايات في هذا المعنى مستفيضة من طرق العامة والخاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects excluding Nimrod’s kingship from God because it was unjust: the Qur’an attributes kingship and wealth even to Pharaoh and Qarun and says all sovereignty belongs to God.
rows.anchor: فما من ملك إلا وهو منه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage depicts Nimrod disputing Abraham’s monotheism and faith, not his right to rule; visible political kingship belonged to Nimrod, so there was no royal claim to contest.
rows.anchor: فإن ظاهرها أن نمرود كان ينازع إبراهيم في توحيده وإيمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kingship, like everything else, has a relation to God, so attributing it to Him presents no difficulty.
rows.anchor: أن لكل شيء نسبة إلى الله سبحانه والملك من جملة الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham may mean animal life and death specifically, or life and death generally; Nimrod’s claim to grant and take life is explained by reports that he released one prisoner and executed another, not by plant cultivation or animal breeding.
rows.anchor: أمر بإحضار رجلين ممن كان في سجنه فأطلق أحدهما وقتل الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham invokes life and death because inert nature cannot produce them, especially conscious, volitional animal life and its opposite, which are nonmaterial.
rows.anchor: وخاصة التي في الحيوان حيث تستتبع الشعور والإرادة، وهما أمران غير ماديين قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod and his audience misunderstood the argument as figurative imprisonment and execution, revealing weak metaphysical understanding; this can coexist with the material achievements of Babylon, Chaldea, and Pharaonic Egypt.
rows.anchor: فإن المدنية المادية أمر والتقدم في معنويات المعارف أمر آخر
